chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: The Vendome Hotel in Buffalo and owner Bill Clore
summary: Horace's Buffalo job was at the Vendome Hotel, not a 'Paramount Inn'. Bill Clore let the starving band play for its rent and later did the same for Jimmie Lunceford's band.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: That's where I got him, in Columbus. Now this particular job that they quoted there in this book of Buffalo, I think is incorrect because we played and stayed in a place there called the Vendome Hotel.
Vendome -- was owned and operated by

a guy named Bill Clore, C-l-o-r-e, which actually turned out to be a legend because we starved to death in that town, and that man let us play for our rent and everything else. And right behind us another band came and started with Jimmie Lunceford, because Willie Smith, the great alto saxophonist told me this, and they stayed -- everybody in two rooms, that big band.

Right there at the Vendome Hotel, and Clore let them play their thing off too. Jimmy Lunceford this was followed behind me, and this particular place where this book has me listed as playing, that's incorrect.
It says the Paramount Inn. You don't --
No, I never heard of it, that wasn't it.
